hints.mcp_fallback:
## If a page will not open

You have MCP tools available in this session for reading web pages, and they are usually stronger than a plain fetch. When a page returns 403, 404, a CAPTCHA, a Cloudflare interstitial, an empty body or a JavaScript-only shell, do NOT give up and do NOT answer from memory. Look at the MCP tools you have available RIGHT NOW - some CLIs load tools lazily and you must issue a tool search first before you can see them - and try whichever one fits the failure. Say in your answer which tool finally worked.

Do NOT fetch or parse a page with the shell (`curl`, `wget`, `python -c`, one-off scripts) unless you have already verified the shell works in this environment. On many CLIs the shell path is either denied by policy (in which case one denied call may discard the whole run) or unable to spawn a subprocess at all - either way, a shell attempt in those cases costs you the run without returning a page. The MCP tools do not go through the shell.

Do NOT use billing-heavy fetchers - anything that bills per page or per token with no ceiling. Prefer free tools; use a metered scrape only as a last resort for a single page. If your session offers a whole-site crawler or an unbounded page-extraction agent, treat those as the meter you are asked to avoid, whatever they are named.

If everything fails, write that the page could not be opened, name what you tried, and tag the claim `[SNIPPET]` or `my search found no confirmation`. A host that refuses automated traffic has given an answer; do not try to defeat it.
hints._generalised_2026_08_08: 🔴 2026-08-08, the operator: «просто скажи, что бы он использовал MCP, а какие именно, не надо, ведь какой-то MCP мог зависнуть и в этот момент не загрузился». Sharper than the earlier «one CLI's tool list differs from another's» that had two paragraphs living where one should have. Availability is DYNAMIC, not static: a server present at install time can be hung, unloaded or filtered out by permissions when the actual call happens - and a named-but-absent tool makes the model report OUR error as its own. That is the same trap that produced the 2026-08-08 morning `NONE` reading for codex, one layer down. The two old paragraphs (`agy_mcp_fallback`, `codex_mcp_fallback`) are GONE; their measurement history is preserved in the `_why` and `_first_reading` notes below, and those notes are now archaeology - the current hint is `mcp_fallback` above, and it names ZERO tools. hints._codex_mcp_fallback_why: 🔴 SUPERSEDED 2026-08-08 by the merger noted above - kept because the CODE OF THE HINT is gone but the MEASUREMENTS are still true and still frame what the merged hint means. 🔴🔴 SUPERSEDES THE 2026-08-08 MORNING CONCLUSION THAT CODEX HAS NO MCP TOOLS. That conclusion came from asking the model («name your MCP page-reading tools») and taking `NONE` as a measurement. It was wrong, and the cause is worth more than the correction: codex-cli 0.147 loads tools LAZILY - the model sees them only after issuing a `tool_search_call` - so «what tools do you have?» is answered from an empty list unless it searches first. Asking a model to enumerate its own tools measures its discovery behaviour, not its tool set. RE-MEASURED the same day, by execution and by the client's own event log rather than by the model's word: `codex mcp list --json` reports NINE configured servers, all `enabled: true`; a probe run produced `mcp_tool_call_end {server: scrapling, tool: fetch}` -> `Ok`, and a second produced `{server: crawl4ai, tool: crawl_url}` -> `Ok`, both returning the real `<h1>` of example.com. 🔴 THE FIRST RE-PROBE WAS ALSO WRONG, in the same direction: after ONE tool search the model reported 3 servers / 20 tools and stated that jina «does not expose read_url». After eleven searches it reported 10 namespaces and 51 tools INCLUDING `read_url` - the first number was the search's `limit`, not the machine's. So even a probe that calls a tool successfully can enumerate the rest wrongly; the enumeration is a self-report at every depth, and only the `mcp_tool_call_end` frames are evidence. That is why the merged hint's first paragraph is about searching rather than about any particular tool. 🔴 Codex also carries `mcp__codex_apps__*` servers (github, tavily_ai, sites) that are NOT in ~/.codex/config.toml - vendor-side apps. They are deliberately not named in the hint: they were seen once, in one model's enumeration, which by the paragraph above is not evidence.
hints._agy_mcp_fallback_why: 🔴 SUPERSEDED 2026-08-08 by the merger noted above - kept for the anti-shell measurement, which is the paragraph the merged hint still carries. 2026-08-08, the operator: «может agy и codex писать доп. текст в промт, что бы они использовали MCP разные для открытия сайтов, если их встроенный fetch не смог открыть сайт?» — YES for agy, and 🔴 YES FOR CODEX TOO since the re-measurement recorded in `_codex_mcp_fallback_why` (the first answer here said NO, on the strength of the model's own `NONE`; that was a self-report, not a measurement, and it was wrong). The old two hints stayed SEPARATE rather than shared because tool names differed, the discovery model differed and the anti-shell paragraph had a different CAUSE on each (agy: a denied command discards the whole run; codex: the sandboxed shell cannot spawn PowerShell at all). 🔴 The 2026-08-08 evening merger reversed that: names dropped, generic wording covers both discovery paths, and the anti-shell paragraph covers both causes in one sentence («denied by policy OR unable to spawn») because dodging shell is the right advice under either. 🔴 The six servers named in the old agy hint were read from ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/mcp.json, not recalled: scrapling, playwright, firecrawl, jina-mcp-server, crawl4ai, cloakbrowser. 🔴 THE ANTI-SHELL PARAGRAPH IS THE REAL PAYLOAD, and it is aimed at a measured failure, not at a hypothetical one: round 27 watched agy die THREE times on three DIFFERENT one-off `python -c` scripts, each denied, each discarding a run that had already made ~29 successful tool calls. The failure is the deep-researcher profile's habit of shelling a fresh script, not a missing page. 🔴 It also goes WITH the grain of a measurement already in this repo: an earlier instruction telling agy to AVOID MCP failed 5/5, because a server's own tool description outranks a system prompt. Pointing it AT the tools it is already pulled toward pushes the same lever the way it already moves - which is why this one is worth trying and that one was not. 🔴 Firecrawl is named ONLY to forbid the unbounded call: the operator's spend policy is enforced by a Claude Code PreToolUse hook, and that hook does not cover agy's own MCP client.
hints._first_reading_2026_08_08: 🟢 FIRST READING, CONSISTENT WITH THE HYPOTHESIS - and it is one reading, not a proof. Round 28, both agy channels, counted from their own stream-json: agy31pro used 2 tools (both search_web); agy36flash used 14 (6 search_web, 4 view_file, 4 call_mcp_tool). `run_command` count: ZERO on both, and both returned status SUCCESS with a full answer - where round 27 had every attempt die on a denied one-off `python -c`. 🔴 WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and the distinction is the whole point: THE BRIEF CHANGED TOO. Round 27's brief was about packages and registries and provoked scripted downloads; round 28's was a design review that did not. Two variables moved, so the honest claim is «no shelling occurred and MCP was used four times», never «the hint prevented shelling». Isolating it costs one round: re-run round 27's brief WITH the hint. Do that before trusting this paragraph. 🔴 It does already correct round 27's other conclusion, that «agy31pro is unusable headless» - it ran fine here, so the failure was never the model.

groups._doc: A word a human types that means SEVERAL channels. Without these, splitting agy into two channels would have broken `--only agy` and «не используй gemini» with 'unknown channel' - the exact defect that made `--only http` unusable for weeks in 2026-07. A group is expanded by routing before anything else runs, so every flag and every free-text route accepts it. Group names and their aliases share one namespace with channel and model aliases, and a collision is refused at load time.

gemini.🔴🔴_SIX_GEMINI_SEATS_IS_A_DECISION_AND_HE:
R43. Two reviewers in the round-42 panel filed «transport deduplication inside a panel» as a defect, and the R42 backlog carried it as an open item on the grounds that a panel's product is DISAGREEMENT and six seats of one vendor are one opinion repeated. the operator answered it directly, and the answer is economic rather than aesthetic - it is recorded here verbatim because it is exactly the kind of premise an outside reviewer cannot see and will therefore keep re-filing:

«у меня подписка через agy и он вообще не тратит токены. Поэтому через него пропускаем все модели подряд, включая 3.1 Pro. А 3.1 Pro по openrouter и напрямую тратил много денег. 3.7 Flash сейчас на скидках, поэтому его везде используем.»

So: (1) the three `agy*` seats are FREE at the margin - a flat subscription, no per-token charge - which is why every Gemini model runs through that transport including 3.1 Pro, the most expensive model in the family. Adding an agy seat costs wall-clock and nothing else. (2) 3.1 Pro exists ONLY on agy for that reason: it was expensive through OpenRouter and through Google's own API, so it has no `orgemini31pro` or `goog31pro` twin and must not acquire one. (3) 3.7 Flash is on vendor discount right now, which is why it is the model that appears on ALL THREE transports (agy37flash, orgemini37flash, goog37flash) rather than one.

🔴 WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISMISS. The vendor-concentration measurement stands and the plan still prints it: cheap = 6 of 11 seats Google. The point is that the concentration is PAID FOR at three different prices, and the seats that make it look worst are the ones that cost nothing. It also does not dismiss the finding that convergence between them is weak evidence - six Geminis agreeing is still one opinion repeated, and a reader should weight it that way. The correct response to that is to read agreement across VENDORS, not to delete free seats. 🔴 AND THE DISCOUNT IS A DATED FACT: «3.7 Flash сейчас на скидках» is true on 2026-08-15 and will stop being true without notice. If the price moves, the argument for three 3.7-Flash transports moves with it - that is a reason to re-read this note, not to trust it.

We believed we were capping a runaway and were in fact running Moonshot's flagship two rungs under its own default, on a channel that is 34.8% of the monthly bill. 🔴 THE T53 REASONING WAS ALSO SUPERSEDED BY A LATER MEASUREMENT and nobody joined them up: the qwen entry's four-arm probe (deliberately tiny 2000-token ceiling, including the arm predicted to starve) showed the effort ratio is a CEILING and not a RESERVATION - every arm returned a complete answer with the marker. kimik3._reasoning_budget: 🔴 On OpenRouter the top-level max_tokens covers REASONING AND ANSWER TOGETHER. That is exactly the 2026-08-03 failure on a 51KB brief: out=32000 exactly, 132,471 reasoning chars, zero answer tokens, no end marker. The mitigation is a GENEROUS max_tokens (the ceiling), not a lowered effort (the depth) - see the probe note on the qwen channel, which tested the alternative and found no evidence for it.

So the sources are often nameable with zero extra requests. _panels_doc:
🔴 A PANEL IS WHO IS IN THE ROOM. A TIER IS HOW DEEP EACH OF THEM GOES. Added 2026-08-15 (round 42), the operator: «Давай теперь разделим оркестр[ацию] на дешевую и стандартную», with the membership he dictated verbatim - «В дешевую добавь: deepseek, Grok, Agy, google и openrouter 3.6 и 3.7 Flash, mimo, nemotron, spark12cont Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor». Everything he did not name stays standard-only: spark11, codex, kimik3, qwen38max, orgpt56terrapro. The two axes are deliberately orthogonal and both print in the plan - `--panel cheap --tier deep` is a legal and sensible combination (few reviewers, each thinking hard), and so is `--panel standard --tier strategic`.

🔴 THE LADDER IS NESTED, NOT A PARTITION: `standard` INCLUDES every cheap channel. «Стандартная» has to mean «what normally runs», and what normally runs is every enabled channel - so `--panel standard` is bit-for-bit the behaviour that shipped before this key existed, and the default is unchanged. A disjoint reading would have produced a four-channel «standard» panel with no Gemini voice at all, which nobody would ever want: the cheap voices cost nothing extra once you are already paying for the expensive ones.

🔴 A PANEL IS NOT A GROUP, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS RESURRECTION. `--only <group>` deliberately overrides `enabled: false` - that is the documented opt-in path. A panel must NOT: it filters DOWN to channels that are already enabled and never turns one on. Implementing `cheap` as a group instead would have been a one-line registry edit and would have been wrong in a way nothing would have caught, because `enabled` is exactly what package.py flips per `distribution`: `--only cheap` in the kit would have resurrected mimo25pro, grok420 and goog36/37flash - four channels whose direct vendor keys a kit user does not have - and here it would have resurrected their OpenRouter twins, paying twice for the same voice. Same word, opposite semantics; they cannot share a mechanism.

🔴 THE NAME `standard` WAS A TIER UNTIL 2026-08-08 AND IS NOT ONE NOW. the operator removed the `quick` and `standard` TIERS that day, and `--tier standard` is still an argparse error naming strategic|deep. The word returning as a PANEL is not that tier coming back - different flag, different axis. Recorded here because the retired name appears in `_tiers_doc` above and a reader meeting both would otherwise be entitled to think one of them is stale.
_panels_hidden_cost_doc: 🔴 THE THING THE CHEAP PANEL COSTS IS VENDOR DIVERSITY, NOT DEPTH - and it is invisible if you only read the price. Counted on this machine 2026-08-15: of the 11 cheap channels enabled here, SIX are Gemini (agy31pro, agy36flash, agy37flash, goog36flash, goog37flash, orgemini37flash). In the generated kit it is five of ten. A panel's whole product is disagreement between independent voices, and six seats sharing one vendor's training data are not six independent voices on a question where that vendor is systematically wrong - they will agree with each other and the convergence will read as corroboration. What `standard` actually buys, therefore, is not «more expensive», it is four more VENDORS: OpenAI (codex), Moonshot (kimik3), Alibaba (qwen38max) and Meta's Standard tier (spark11). The plan prints the vendor breakdown of whatever set resolves, so this is checkable at run time rather than trusted from this paragraph.
_default_panel_is_cheap_SINCE_2026_08_16:
Flipped 2026-08-16 (R45) on the operator's instruction «Дефолт сделай на дешевые», after being offered and declined in R42 and R44. WHAT THE OLD NOTE FEARED, kept because it names the real cost: a cheaper default silently removes codex, kimik3, qwen38max and spark11 from every round launched with no flag - including legal rounds in another project, where the loss is four VENDORS on a question with a filing deadline. A default that quietly spends more is a bug; a default that quietly reviews LESS is also a bug, and the second is harder to notice.

WHY IT IS SAFE TO TAKE NOW, and this is a property of the code rather than a promise: the plan printer is SYMMETRIC. It already prints «--panel standard would ALSO run: codex, kimik3, qwen38max, spark11» on every cheap run, by name, from the same `gain`/`lose` computation that used to print the drop list on standard runs. So the loss the old note called invisible is printed before anything is spent, on every single round, and a reader who wants the four vendors back is told the exact flag. Verified by reading routing.py's panel block, not assumed from the fact that a feature with that name exists.

🔴 WHAT STILL BITES, said plainly: this changes the default for OTHER PROJECTS' scripts too, and a script that passed no --panel now gets 4 vendors fewer without being edited. The mitigation is the printed line, not a guarantee - if a caller pipes the plan to a file nobody reads, the loss is silent again. Pass `--panel standard` explicitly in anything whose value depends on vendor breadth.

cheap.label: cheap panel
cheap._aliases_and_the_two_things_that_are_NOT: «дешёвая» needs no entry: both the panel extractor and the entity scanner fold ё to е before matching, the same normalisation the route parser has always used. Case endings DO need entries, because nothing stems Russian here - «дешевой» is not derivable from «дешевая» by any rule this file implements. 🔴 WHAT A MISSING ENDING ACTUALLY DOES, CORRECTED 2026-08-15 after a reviewer traced it: this note used to say it «falls through to default_panel», which is only half the story and the reassuring half. If the rest of the route names a channel («не используй grok на дешевом»), the panel word is invisible and the round runs the DEFAULT - i.e. the expensive - panel, silently. If it names nothing («запусти на дешевом»), the route dies with «no channel or model in this route matched the registry», an error about the wrong thing entirely. Neither outcome is the one asked for, and one of them costs money. That is why this list is longer than it looks like it needs to be, and why the endings a Russian speaker would actually type were added by asking a panel rather than by introspection.
cheap._what_it_is: Every channel that is either free, on a flat-rate subscription, or metered below roughly $1/M input. Subscriptions (agy) count as cheap because their marginal cost is zero, even though the weekly allowance is a real and scarce resource - which is why `codex`, also a subscription, is NOT here: it is rationed for a different reason (slow, strategic-only), and that policy predates this key.
cheap._the_seat_it_loses: kimik3 carries `role: code` and is standard-only, so the cheap panel would have had no code voice at all. ordeepseekv4pro was added in the same round and carries `role: code` for exactly that reason. See _panels_hidden_cost_doc for the loss that is NOT filled by anything: four vendors.

standard.label: standard panel
standard.🔴_ВСЕ_MEANS_THIS_PANEL_AND_UNTIL_R43_IT_:
the operator asked, R43: «как я понял, что бы их вызвать надо писать именно определенные слова или claude code сам понимает, если ему сказать запусти дешевые или запусти все?» - and the honest answer was half-bad. «запусти дешевые» worked; «запусти все» was a ROUTE ERROR («no channel or model in this route matched the registry»), because `все` named nothing. The most natural way to ask for everything was the one sentence the router could not read.

🔴 WHY THIS IS SAFE WHERE `full` WAS NOT. `full` was removed in R42 because it answers the OTHER AXIS - «run a full analysis» is asking about DEPTH, and the panel extractor was eating it. `все` cannot make that mistake for two independent reasons: it is not a depth word in either language, and since R43 there IS no depth axis to confuse it with - one tier, always the ceiling. The remaining risk is that `все` is simply a very common Russian word, and that is answered by what happens when it is eaten wrongly: «не используй все openrouter модели» becomes «не используй openrouter модели», which is the same instruction; and a leftover with no instruction in it is filler, which resolve() now tolerates. A leftover WITH a marker and no channel still raises.

🔴 AND WHAT `все` MUST NOT DO: wake Terra Pro. the operator's rule is that «запусти все» excludes it and only «Запусти все, включая Terra pro» includes it. That holds mechanically rather than by this paragraph - `explicit_only` blocks every panel, and the ADD word «включая» is what makes his authorising sentence parse at all (it did not, before R43).
standard.🔴_words_that_could_mean_DEPTH_are_not_pa: `full`, `полная`, `полную`, `полной` were here and are GONE, and the reason is sharper than «too common». A bare word is dangerous as a panel alias exactly when it could equally name the OTHER axis: «run a full analysis», «полная проверка» are asking for THOROUGHNESS, which is `--tier deep`, not for a room full of reviewers. Measured 2026-08-15, before the removal: `--route "run a full analysis with grok"` silently set panel=standard AND swallowed the word, so the leftover produced «'run a  analysis with grok' mentions grok420 but no instruction word» - the wrong action taken, and an error message about something else. `full panel` and `полная панель` stay, because the noun disambiguates. Two reviewers found this independently. The general rule for anyone adding an alias here: ask whether the word could be an answer to «how deep», not just whether it is common.
standard._what_it_is: Every enabled channel - the behaviour that shipped before panels existed, and the default. Adds spark11 (Meta Standard tier, no training grant), codex (OpenAI via the ChatGPT subscription, strategic questions only), kimik3 (Moonshot, the code voice) and qwen38max (Alibaba). orgpt56terrapro is nominally in this panel and still does not run without `--only` plus `--accept-spend`: `panel` and `enabled` answer different questions, and a panel never resurrects a default-off channel.

_tiers_doc: 🔴 TWO TIERS SINCE 2026-08-08, and the reason is a question that had no good answer. the operator: «quick и standart tier давай уберем. И не понятно визуально, чем отличается strategic от Deep.» He was right, and the honest answer was embarrassing: strategic and deep differed by NOTHING except a timeout - identical agy_effort, identical http_effort - so a human reading the two words was promised a depth difference the file did not contain. Rather than invent one, `deep` now changes the three things that CAN change on every vendor (time, pages read, room to think) and the plan PRINTS the resolved value per channel, including «already at this vendor's ceiling, deep changes nothing here». A tier is a word; what it resolves to has to be visible before anything is spent. 🔴 quick and standard are GONE, not hidden: `--tier quick` is now an argparse error naming the two that exist, because a silently-accepted dead tier is the decorative-knob defect this file keeps recording. 🔴 THE TIER LIST HAS ONE HOME. Until 2026-08-08 it had two - this object AND a `TIERS` dict in orchestrate.py that fed `--tier`'s choices - so deleting a tier here would have left the flag still accepting it and falling through to defaults. orchestrate now derives its tiers from this file. HISTORY, kept because each entry is a lever that was wired to nothing: codex_timeout added 2026-08-05 (before it, codex fell through to a hard-coded 3000 s while the harness advised 'raise the timeout for that channel', naming a lever that did not exist); http_effort added 2026-08-06 (the tier varied `thinking.budget_tokens`, which Meta documents as «accepted for compatibility but not translated into an effort value» - depth is output_config.effort alone, which the code pinned at xhigh for every tier, so the ladder did nothing on Spark). PROBED 2026-08-06 on both Spark models: low/medium/high/xhigh all return 200, `max` returns 400 on both, and so does an invented value - the negative control proving the endpoint validates the field. xhigh is the real ceiling even though Meta's own OpenAPI enum lists `max`.
_tiers_reach_correction_2026_08_15: 🔴 «AND EVERY OPENROUTER/OAI CHANNEL (REASONING CEILING AND PAGE-FETCH BUDGET, BOTH MULTIPLIED)» IN THE NEXT KEY IS TOO STRONG, and three of eight reviewers caught it on the same day. The multiplier acts on `reasoning.max_tokens`; a channel that declares `reasoning.effort` INSTEAD has no number to multiply, so `deep` moves only its fetch budget. That is true today of `ordeepseekv4pro` (effort high, two rungs) and of `ornemotron3ultra` (effort high). The plan has always printed the truth per channel - «nothing this tier can raise on this channel» - so the code was right and the prose generalised. Kept as a correction beside the original rather than edited into it, because the original sentence is the measurement of 2026-08-08 and rewriting a measurement to match a later one is how a record stops being a record. The fix that would make the sentence true again is a raise-only effort rule clamped to each model's declared ladder; deferred, because an absolute tier effort would silently DOWNGRADE qwen38max, which already runs xhigh.
_tiers_reach_doc: 🔴 WHICH CHANNELS THE TIER ACTUALLY REACHES, measured 2026-08-08 rather than assumed. Before this round the answer was 4 of 11 - two Spark and two agy - while `--tier` read like a global control. Now: agy (effort+timeout), codex (timeout only; its effort is pinned in its own block and the subscription has no cheaper setting worth having), http/Spark (effort+thinking budget+output floor), gemini (thinking_level - see goog36flash, this was believed impossible until the docs were re-read), and every openrouter/oai channel (reasoning ceiling and page-fetch budget, both multiplied). xai gets the timeout and nothing else. 🔴🔴 TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT LAST CLAUSE, both from the round-29 panel reviewing this very change, and both right. (a) codex noticed the dispatcher passed NO timeout to the xai channel at all - `call_xai_responses` fell back to its own 2400 s default in both tiers - so `deep` was a literal NO-OP there while the printed note claimed it bought wall-clock. A line written to be honest about a missing lever was itself wrong about the one lever that remained. Fixed: it now takes `codex_timeout`. (b) qwen38max objected that «no depth knob on this vendor» rested on a single 400 from a single placement - the exact error this round had just corrected for Gemini - and cited xAI's own docs showing `reasoning_effort` on grok-4.5 and `reasoning.effort` on grok-4.20-multi-agent. RE-PROBED on /v1/responses in the Responses shape: `reasoning:{"effort":"low"|"high"|"zzz"}` ALL return `400 Model grok-4.20-0309-reasoning does not support parameter reasoningEffort`, identical to the top-level placement, while the invented sibling `reasoning:{"effort_zzz":"low"}` returns 200 and is silently ignored. The refusal is MODEL-level, not a placement mistake, so the correct wording is «this model», never «this vendor». The objection was methodologically right and changed the sentence even though it did not change the outcome - which is what a panel is for.
🔴🔴_ONE_TIER_SINCE_2026_08_15_R43_AND_THE:
the operator, R43: «у нас только должны отличаться количество моделей, а мозги у всех режимов должны быть на максимум». One axis survives as a CHOICE - the panel, i.e. who is in the room. Depth is no longer a choice: every channel runs at the ceiling its own vendor declares, in every mode, always.

WHY THIS IS A DELETION AND NOT A RENAME. `strategic` and `deep` differed, on the day they were collapsed, in exactly four values: agy 25m->40m, codex 50m->75m, Spark's inert thinking budget 60k->100k with its output FLOOR 15k->25k, and two multipliers. Depth was identical on agy (high is the model ceiling), on Spark (xhigh, `max` returns 400 - re-probed 2026-08-15 with an invented value as the negative control), on gemini (high is the top of thinking_levels) and on xai (this model refuses reasoningEffort at every value and placement). So the pair had already decayed back into «a timeout», which is the exact defect the operator named on 2026-08-08 and which `deep` was rebuilt to cure. It came back because the cure was a multiplier over per-channel values, and the per-channel values kept moving to their ceilings. A knob whose range shrinks to a point every time the underlying values improve is not a knob.

WHAT THE OLD NAMES DO NOW: `--tier strategic` and `--tier deep` are ALIASES of `max` and still parse, so nothing anyone has typed before - including the scripts in the other project - breaks. The plan prints «tier: max (you asked for 'deep'; there is one tier now and it is the ceiling)» rather than accepting the word in silence, because a flag accepted and not applied is this project's most expensive recurring class. `--tier quick` is still an argparse error.

WHAT WAS *NOT* RAISED, SAID OUT LOUD: (1) `fetch_tool.max_calls` was 8 and is 11 per channel since 2026-08-16 (R45), on the operator's instruction «Бюджет страниц поставь 11». The reason the old note gave for holding at 8 was that one 400 KB page cost 273 018 input tokens in R42 and that raising the call count raises that exposure on every round forever. 🔴 THAT REASONING WAS WRONG ABOUT WHICH KNOB BOUNDS THE RUNAWAY, and it is corrected here rather than deleted: the worst case is bounded by BYTES, not by CALLS. `FETCH_RUN_BUDGET` (1 000 000 bytes, cumulative per channel per review, added 2026-08-08 for exactly this failure) stops the loop after roughly two and a half maximum-size pages no matter how many calls remain, and `FETCH_MAX_BYTES` truncates any single page at 400 KB. So the three extra calls buy more SMALL pages - which is the case that actually helps, since a primary source read is what separates a verified citation from an invented one - and they cannot multiply the token-bomb ceiling, because that ceiling was never a function of the call count. Verified by reading both constants, not assumed. (2) `http_floor` stays 15000, NOT the 25000 `deep` used: the floor is a WARNING threshold on output size, and every real Spark output measured here (10 947 / 18 307 / 18 841 / 20 464) sits below 25000, so `deep` was arming a false alarm on every round that used it. A threshold that fires on correct behaviour trains the reader to ignore it.

max._what_it_is: The only tier. Every vendor at the maximum depth it will accept, verified per channel rather than assumed - see `_depth_ceilings_measured` below for what each ceiling is and how it was established. The values here are the per-KIND ones; the per-CHANNEL ones (reasoning.effort, thinking_level, max_tokens) live in each channel's own block, which is the single home for them.
max._aliases_why: `strategic` and `deep` are here so that every command anyone has ever run keeps working and resolves to the ceiling. They are aliases, not tiers: `python routing.py --tier deep` prints the same plan as `--tier max` and says which word it honoured.
max._timeouts_took_the_GENEROUS_values_on_pu: 40m/75m, which is what `deep` used, not what `strategic` did. This is a consequence of the depth change rather than a separate decision: raising every ceiling makes every call potentially longer. mimo25pro already spent 766 seconds filling a 60 000-token budget; at 131 072 the same brief can run past agy's old 25-minute wall. Raising the caps and leaving the clocks would have converted a truncation into a timeout and called it progress.
max._gemini_thinking_level_note: Raised medium->high on 2026-08-08 at the operator's instruction, after measuring it rather than before (goog36flash._thinking_level_default: medium 1635 thought tokens against high 1963, non-overlapping ranges over 3 interleaved samples each). `high` is the top of this channel's declared `thinking_levels`, so it is the ceiling and not a preference.
max._http_thinking_budget_is_SENT_AND_INERT: Meta documents `thinking.budget_tokens` as «accepted for compatibility but not translated into an effort value»; depth on that endpoint is `output_config.effort` alone, which is pinned at xhigh here. The field is still sent at the larger of the two historical values because it costs nothing and would become real if the vendor ever wires it. It is listed here as inert rather than quietly dropped, so nobody re-derives it as a depth lever later.
max._the_two_multipliers_are_GONE: `or_reasoning_scale` and `fetch_scale` were removed with the second tier. With one tier a multiplier is an obfuscated constant living in the wrong file: it took a per-channel value and changed it from somewhere the channel's own block could not show. The two channels that actually had a number to multiply (ormimo25pro, orgrok420 - both kit-only) now declare 48 000 directly, which is exactly what `deep` used to compute for them, so no kit user loses depth in the collapse.

_max_tokens_rule_two_channels_NOT_covere: 🔴 goog36flash AND goog37flash STAY AT 60000, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE NUMBER WAS NOT ESTABLISHED - not that 60000 was chosen. Their OpenRouter twins report `max_completion_tokens: 65536` and were raised to it; copying that across would be the exact mistake this registry records under `_is_not_the_same_channel_as_mimo25pro` and under [[transport-beats-model]] - a limit measured on one transport is not a limit on another. The probe run for it on 2026-08-15 asked the WRONG ENDPOINT (`:generateContent` with `thinkingLevel` in `generation_config`) and got `400 Unknown name "thinkingLevel"` at every value including 60000, which proves only that the probe was wrong: these channels talk to `/v1beta/interactions`, where the field is `generation_config.thinking_level`. So the ceiling on the direct transport is UNKNOWN and is written down as unknown. 🔴 It also matters less here than anywhere else: on this transport `candidatesTokenCount` EXCLUDES thinking (measured r42: out 5 298 beside 16 423 thought tokens), so the shared-ceiling exhaustion this round is about does not apply in the same way - and the largest real answer either channel has produced is ~11% of 60 000. Raising it would buy nothing measurable; establishing the real number is a one-probe task for the next round.
_max_tokens_rule:
🔴 ONE RULE FOR EVERY CHANNEL'S `max_tokens`, SET IN R43: **min(the vendor's own declared max_completion_tokens, 131072)**, and where the vendor declares none, 131072. Resolved values: mimo25pro 131072 (vendor 400 says «at most 131072»), grok420 131072, kimik3 131072 (no declared cap), qwen38max 131072 (vendor 131072), ormimo25pro 131072, orgrok420 131072, ordeepseekv4pro 131072 (vendor allows 393216 - the cap here is OURS), orgemini36flash 65536, orgemini37flash 65536, ornemotron3ultra 65536 (all three the vendor's own ceiling).

WHY A CEILING OF OUR OWN AT ALL, when the point of this round is maximum depth: on these protocols `max_tokens` bounds REASONING AND ANSWER TOGETHER, so it is simultaneously the depth allowance and the only backstop against a pathological trace. 131072 is the largest value this project has both sent successfully and seen approached - mimo filled 60 000 of it on a single heavy brief - while 393 216 is a number nothing here has ever come near and which would let one stuck channel bill four times the worst case already measured. Raising it further is a decision to take when a real run is truncated at 131072, and that has never happened.

🔴 THE ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION: orgpt56terrapro stays at 120000 against a declared 128000. It is the channel with the only measured runaway in this project's history ($12.08 in one round), it is now both opt-in and explicit-only, and the operator's standing instruction is that it must not be exercised. Leaving 8 000 tokens on the table on a channel nobody may run is not an oversight; changing a locked channel unasked would be.
